title: Saving Democracy Requires Taxing Extreme Wealth
gist: A teaser arguing that wealth-tax design research has advanced far enough to avoid the failures of earlier European attempts, using SpaceX's June IPO — which briefly made Elon Musk the world's first trillionaire — as evidence that dynastic wealth concentration has become a democratic emergency.

themes.theme: The First Trillionaire and the SpaceX IPO

insights.claim: Following SpaceX's IPO in June 2026, Elon Musk briefly became the world's first trillionaire, making him wealthier than the poorest 46% of the world's people combined.
insights.speaker: MICHAEL MADOWITZ
insights.so_what: The SpaceX listing is the single largest wealth-creation event on record and now anchors the political case for a US wealth tax — a policy risk to concentrated founder stakes.
insights.quote: Following SpaceX’s IPO in June, Elon Musk briefly became the world’s first trillionaire, making him wealthier than the poorest 46% of the world’s people combined.

insights.claim: Elon Musk's wealth has more than tripled since the 2024 US presidential election.
insights.speaker: MICHAEL MADOWITZ
insights.so_what: A 3x gain concentrated in the post-2024 political cycle is the empirical hook that makes proximity to power look like an investable — and taxable — factor.
insights.quote: His wealth has more than tripled since the 2024 presidential election
insights.locator: His wealth has more than tripled

themes.theme: Political Spending as Return on Capital

insights.claim: Elon Musk spent roughly $290 million supporting Donald Trump's 2024 candidacy — more than double what Trump raised from small donors.
insights.speaker: MICHAEL MADOWITZ
insights.so_what: When one individual outspends an entire small-donor base by 2x, policy outcomes become a function of a handful of balance sheets — raising both regulatory-capture upside and eventual backlash risk.
insights.quote: he spent roughly $290 million to support Donald Trump’s candidacy—more than double what the president raised from small donors

insights.claim: Lawmakers can now draw on considerable research designing a wealth tax that avoids the pitfalls that defeated other countries' earlier attempts.
insights.speaker: MICHAEL MADOWITZ
insights.so_what: The technical-infeasibility objection to wealth taxes is being retired, which raises the medium-term probability of US wealth-tax legislation clearing design scrutiny.
insights.quote: they can draw on considerable research that has gone into designing a wealth tax that avoids the pitfalls of other countries’ attempts
